canonical_decimal.scope: Only declared canonical-decimal counters consult this rule. gen_ai.audio.bytes keeps full canonical decimal strings with a safe-integer numeric value unless they have base64 shape at or above base64_min_chars. elevenlabs.audio.bytes never grants a string role. The four-character shape threshold is not a special case for one count. Preserve accepted string types; no signs, leading zeros, fractions, exponents, whitespace or final newline. Other G4 core/detail keys retain their original scalar roles, including arbitrary strings and literal undefined. This rule does not change Q8b NON_CONTENT types.

scalar_metrics.scope: Closed exact complete keys in the declared usage/metrics containers only. Case, punctuation, prefixes, suffixes and array indices are not aliases. A nested object path must equal the complete key. gen_ai.audio and elevenlabs.audio are metric containers only for their listed bytes counters, not for arbitrary audio members. Their nonnegative_safe_integer value_type grants a role to finite nonnegative safe-integer numbers; only gen_ai.audio.bytes additionally accepts strings under canonical_decimal. gen_ai.usage.cache_read_tokens.audio and the legacy llm.token_count.prompt_details.audio / llm.token_count.completion_details.audio counters also accept only nonnegative safe-integer numbers, never strings. All other inputs on these typed counters retain the role-free media policy. Other declared metrics keep their original number/boolean/string roles without decimal validation.
scalar_metrics.precedence: Scalar role only removes structural media classification caused by the metric spelling. Explicit media/type hints on any ancestor, inherited media/audio, established media payload ancestry, credential ancestry and known numeric/string secrets take precedence. On the two typed byte counters only, base64-shaped strings at or above canonical_decimal.base64_min_chars cannot obtain a role, even when numerically safe. Magic bytes, data URIs and other independent value checks still apply. A counter leaf under established media payload ancestry cannot use the usage metadata boundary to escape omission. Private payload-role ancestry survives parsed, stringified and diagnostic JSON handoffs; resetting a JSON root never grants a metric role. Metric-looking descendants reached through this retained payload origin remain payload, including numeric/bool scalars and numeric/bool arrays; ordinary metadata text boundaries are unchanged.
scalar_metrics.arrays: Arrays never receive the scalar metric role. Nonempty numeric/bool media payload arrays are omitted; existing string/object array walking and empty-array behavior remain unchanged.

zero_detail_deferral.scope: Only these exact keys with numeric value zero may minimally yield to canonical output and its earlier output groups. Nonzero, string-zero, unknown usage, core totals and identity remain protected. Deferred counters are metadata, not dropped content.

normalization.paths: Split dotted and bracket-indexed paths into components; ignore numeric indices. Test every component, retaining credential ancestry. Also test the folded full name unless a component is explicitly excluded. An excluded metric component never exempts a different credential component.

source_ownership.registered_matches: Match original text before independent owners or syntax rewrites. Preserve minimum eight characters, longest-first matching and replacement-sentinel segments. A crossing match consumes the affected complete JSON/string owner and overlapping prose bytes; never restore bare-media scanning over reconstructed URL/JSON syntax.
source_ownership.json_reuse: Never reuse raw duplicate members merely because surviving parsed values compare equal. Nonnumeric discarded values force sanitized rendering. Retained numeric/sentinel duplicates require every original numeric occurrence to pass its full path, MIME, payload and source-lexeme policy; fixed sentinels are checked for registered substrings. Preserve unrelated original numeric lexemes in every structural edit. Raw escaped registered strings are redacted at their source owner, not by injecting unescaped markers into JSON.

exclusions.reason: Token limits, usage and singular/plural token-detail objects and their counters are not authentication tokens. Independent credential markers still win; this is not a blanket subtree exemption.
Token timing and throughput measurements are numeric metadata, not credentials. Independent credential markers still win, including in the same component; no blanket subtree exemption.
Explicit non-secret usage and tokenizer metadata; not a blanket usage subtree exemption.
Identifiers, not the corresponding private key material. x-amz-credential remains secret. Access-key identifiers are masked for the manual Mastra privacy contract.
Explicit metadata and ordinary words; never arbitrary *key* exemptions.
Avoid the sig substring in ordinary words and signing-algorithm metadata.
Session metrics, not session identifiers or session cookies.
Cookie configuration and counts, not Cookie/Set-Cookie values.

value_shapes.reason: Bare long provider-key shape; applies to values, never an exemption.
Credential authorization scheme and value, including unnamed logprob values.
Complete or truncated private-key PEM value.

signed_url.decode_parameter_names: Before treating a scalar/body/attribute/array-element value as one HTTP(S), /path or ?query URL, validate its entire lexical boundary, not only its prefix. A message beginning with a URL can still be prose containing later URLs: scan every URL independently and preserve the prose. Recognized data-URI query values own literal quotes, whitespace, markup and backslashes; mask only those payloads for whole-URL lexical validation, then parse the original whole URL before delimiter-limited scanning. Never use credential or audio redaction to validate the boundary, since it can swallow prose or later URLs. Isolate each HTTP(S) URL or relative /path or ?query reference in text. Apostrophes are legal URI characters in names and values, not token delimiters; preserve enclosing single quotes in prose. Split off the fragment before splitting at the first question mark; later question marks are legal query-name/value characters. Split query pairs on ampersands, then the first equals sign. Percent-decode names once as UTF-8; plus means space. Use the same predicate as transport observation. Percent-decode values once and apply the shared structural media predicate, including data-URI recognition, not only base64 sniffing. Treat all decoded query pairs as one flat object for MIME/type siblings, including dotted/bracket-indexed names and duplicate hints (combine hints, never last-value-wins); keep exact indexed parent isolation. Frame query pairs before scanning literal data URIs so following parameters/fragments survive. Do not recursively decode nested URLs. Preserve original spelling of unchanged values, separators, ordering, duplicates and fragments; replace only sensitive values. Already-redacted values are stable.

media.length_counts: ASCII characters in the original payload including CR/LF; data URI payload is percent-decoded once before counting.

data_uri.scheme_boundary: The character before data: must not be an ASCII letter, digit, plus, dot, hyphen, underscore or colon. Never match the data: suffix of metadata: or another scheme/name.
data_uri.value_boundary: When an exact scalar/body/attribute/array-element or decoded query value begins with data: and contains a comma, the entire value is the URI. Quotes, apostrophes, whitespace, brackets and embedded URLs are payload, never delimiters. Recognize it before contextual media rules. Only free text uses delimiter-limited scanning; a prefix without a comma is not a data URI.

mime_siblings.scope: The same object's payload fields and all their descendants, including source/inlineData wrappers. Payload ancestry persists through arbitrary chunk wrappers and numeric indices. Audio metadata_fields reset inherited media, audio and payload context at that component, so transcript.content is text. Fresh explicit hints/fields can start new context beneath a boundary. For flattened siblings use the exact indexed parent path; never bleed into another array element. Scalar, string-array and indexed MIME hints bind to the MIME field's parent, not its index. MIME parameters after a semicolon are ignored.

image.scope: Type, modality and image MIME siblings establish image context in the same object and its descendants. Existing generic MIME payload fields retain their policy. These additional image payload fields omit encoded values at any length, including image_url and url, while ordinary HTTP URLs remain text. Audio metadata boundaries still reset inherited context except when the component is itself an image payload field. Exact indexed parents isolate sibling hints. No magic-signature or positive-cap exemption is added.

video.scope: Type and modality video declarations establish the same generic media context as video MIME siblings. The mime_siblings payload_fields and their descendants are omitted at every image cap, even without a magic signature. Audio metadata boundaries and exact indexed-parent isolation remain unchanged. This adds no safe-MIME evidence and does not extend image-only URL payload fields to video.

audio.scope: An audio field's direct scalar or indexed/array samples are payload, but an audio object establishes only audio context for its named children. Only explicit payload fields start inherited payload context through arbitrary wrappers. Keep direct-sample context separate from established payload ancestry: a nested audio field never clears that ancestry; only metadata_fields do. When a field is both an audio field and a MIME payload field (audio_base64), both rules apply, so MIME-established payload ancestry persists through its named wrappers. Parameters such as voice, format, max_tokens, sample_rate, speed, IDs and usage are not implicitly payload. Type hints establish audio context, not payload. Credential, magic-byte and data-URI rules still apply independently.
audio.numeric_arrays: Replace numeric/bool payload scalars or arrays with other_replacement; walk arrays of strings/objects preserving structure. Null and empty arrays carry no media bytes.

scope: S6 recognition only. SDK S1 snapshot/hide-family and S5 process-wide registry/transport observation are mandatory in addition; this catalog does not redefine registry timing or permit body buffering on suppressed requests.

logprob_tokens.disclosure: logprob tokens are checked against registered secrets and credential shapes, not key-name rules
logprob_tokens.anchor: Explicit parsed provider response root only; never generic attributes, tool results, user content, nested JSON strings or flattened key spellings. Wildcards require real arrays.
logprob_tokens.reconstruction: If value masking changes any choice message.content or delta.content, fully mask its entire logprobs block. Buffered streams are scanned by choice index before export: earlier, current and later blocks are masked, including top_logprobs and bytes. Concatenated deltas are checked too; affected streaming text is fully masked. No raw delta is exported before this scan.

formats.provider_equivalents: Only the same OpenAI chat response structure is evidenced; no additional provider-specific token paths are registered.
